The maintainer's repository description identifies a rust-analyzer crash reproducer; no README was available.
Python task runner for Zebra CI checks, not the Zebra node.

End-to-end test suite for Zaino, rather than the indexing service.
Survey of existing wallet export formats, not an implemented protocol or the migration tool itself.
TypeScript RPC client package, not an RPC server or indexer.
Deployment and monitoring stack for a zcashd metrics exporter.
Rust client bindings for the Ledger Zcash application, separate from the device wallet application.

Despite the SDK name, the README describes a Cosmos/CometBFT application-specific voting chain with the svoted chain binary, validator startup, REST endpoints and an ABCI vote module. Its repository purpose is voting infrastructure, not a general Zcash node or merely a client SDK.
The README explicitly identifies the circuit-only layer: delegation, vote and share-reveal proofs. Wallets normally use a higher-level crate; this repository implements cryptographic circuits.

The workspace synchronizes nullifiers, builds a proof dataset and serves encrypted PIR queries. It includes cryptographic and client libraries, but the documented end-to-end deliverable is a data-retrieval service with a production deployment runbook.

The current workspace has one member, zcvlib, whose manifest describes it as a Rust library for coin-weighted voting. It provides reusable client/server features and creator, voter, counter and CometBFT binaries. Library is the primary published unit; installation documentation also covers its voting validator server.
The README builds Docker images and runs coordinator/validator services and their CometBFT election chain. This is deployment infrastructure for voting, not wallet or generic application code.

Cargo declares the zcash-warpsync package and warp_api_ffi rlib, with Dart/native bindings and optional wallet/RPC binaries. README methods include wallet creation, balances, history and payments. Voting is one consumer, not its primary purpose.

This is a fork of the general Namada Layer-1 codebase. The README documents installing a node, client and wallet and describes CometBFT consensus, MASP and IBC. Its relationship to Zair does not turn the full node repository into a proof or airdrop library. Tags explicitly identify Namada, so it is not presented as a Zcash consensus node.

Reconciled the 84-item derived grant review queue against the complete approved set. That queue is category triage, not an authority for current approval, delivery, payment, or app completeness.

Repository links were collected from exact grant applications, maintainer progress reports, canonical project documentation, and live GitHub owner/repository metadata. Renewals are grouped by project, while each approval or later decision remains a separate event.

Repository scope is selected for every GitHub owner. This excludes unrelated multi-chain, non-Zcash, personal, fork, and newer DarkFi projects; a whole organization is never automatically labelled grant-funded.

GitHub aliases were resolved to current canonical nameWithOwner values, including Eiger to Equilibrium, pacu to zecdev, zpublish to zecpublish, and runziggurat/zcash-gui to runziggurat/ziggurat-viz. ZecHub and hito-dev are GitHub User accounts.

Historical ledger dates are not assumed to be actual decision dates. When a ledger date predates the primary proposal, date is null and ledgerRecordedDate is retained. Some early ledger entries repeat July 13, 2021; further chronology reconciliation remains useful.

WebZjs retains the initial and subsequent historical approvals separately from the declined 2026 renewal. The public Noir dApp SDK is not the full wallet extension and is not proof of completed WalletConnect integration.

Education/documentation, research prototypes, operational services, legal work, events, marketing, travel, and liquidity support are classified explicitly and are not all turned into software-app cards.
ZGo, Zenith, Arti, Maya, and StageX use non-GitHub source hosts. Full primary repository URLs are retained; no GitHub activity statistics should be fabricated for those hosts.

Coverage is a source-confirmed public-code catalogue for the reviewed ZCG/Coinholder universe, not proof that every grantee repository, private implementation, pre-ZCG Foundation grant, abandoned URL, or non-code deliverable has been discovered. Unverified software candidates remain in unresolved.

Free2Z legal-expense reimbursement is a non-software accounting item in the derived queue, not a new app. Bootstrap/ECC's Coinholder keyholder-veto item is not added as an approved grantee project; organizational funding research is separate.

mergeInto maps equivalent records in the separate coverage/seed inventories; relatedProjectIds marks parent/component overlap without asserting a one-to-one app equivalence. LedgerHQ's later integration uses ledger-hq-zcash and must not be conflated with Zondax's ledger-zcash coverage record.
